1.5 An equimolar mixture of tryptophan ($\mathbf{A}$, pI = 5.88), histidine ($\mathbf{B}$, pI = 7.6) and aspartic acid ($\mathbf{C}$, pI = 2.98) was made in a buffer solution of pH = 6.0. This mixture was poured into column of $\mathbf{X}$. The order in which these amino acids will come out of the column is (Mark X in the correct box)

• i) $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$
• ii) $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$
• iii) $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{A}$
• iv) $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{B}$
• v) $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{A}$
• vi) $\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{C}$

Part II

Keratin (hair protein) contains unusually large number of cysteine units. These units from different part of the protein chains on mild oxidation form disulphide linkages which are responsible for the 3-D structure of hair.

$$\ce{2R-SH ->[(O)] R-S-S-R + 2H+ + 2e-}$$

Curling or straightening of hair involves rearranging these $\ce{-S-S-}$ linkages of keratin.

Thus, the amino acids with mercapto (thiol) groups can act as reducing agents.

1.6 a. The simplest β-mercapto-α-amino acid reduces Cu(II) ions to Cu(I). Write a balanced chemical equation for this reaction.

Compound $\mathbf{P}$, a β-mercapto α-amino acid with one chiral centre, is a biochemical breakdown product of the antibiotic penicillin. Excess of $\mathbf{P}$ when reacted with copper(II) chloride at its pI (6.2) gives a yellow precipitate of compound $\mathbf{Q}$. Elemental analysis showed that $\mathbf{Q}$ contains 26.14% C, 5.26% H and 27.66% Cu. The compound $\mathbf{Q}$ (molar mass = $229.5\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) also has one water molecule of hydration.

b. Deduce the molecular formula of $\mathbf{Q}$ showing the appropriate steps.

c. Draw the structure of $\mathbf{P}$.

Wilson's disease is a genetic disease of copper assimilation in humans. This condition is effectively treated using agents such as $\mathbf{P}$ that can chelate copper. Lewis bases like thioethers and thioelates make stable complexes with Cu(I) with 2 to 4 coordination at the metal center, in preference to Cu(II) ions. However, Cu(II) ions gives 4 to 6 co-ordinations with Lewis bases like amino, amido and carbonyl oxygen.

d. Write the balanced chemical equation(s) for the reaction of $\mathbf{P}$ (excess) with copper(II) chloride at its pI = 6.2 leading to the formation of $\mathbf{Q}$.

Part III: Thyroxine

Thyroid hormones are derivatives of the amino acid tyrosine having iodine bound covalently to aromatic carbon atoms. There are two thyroid hormones: the principal one is thyroxine. Thyroxine's chemical structure was deciphered in 1927 and was found to be optically active, but its stereochemical configuration was difficult to decipher. In 1934, researchers of Pathological Chemistry in a medical college in London were able to get the configuration of Thyroxine by the following method based on L-tyrosine.

An aqueous solution of thyroxine ($\ce{C15H11O4NI4}$) on treatment with $\ce{Pd/CaCO3}$ in an atmosphere of $\ce{H2}$ also gave the same compound $\mathbf{Z}$ on workup (the reaction mixture on acidification and evaporation). This $\mathbf{Z}$ had the same specific rotation as when obtained from L-tyrosine.

problems.title: Boron Compounds through the Ages
problems.problem:
Problem 2 (17 marks). Boron Compounds through the Ages

Boron has been widely found in nature in form of Borax, known as "Buraq" in Arabic, suhaga in Hindi, and tankan in Sanskrit. In 1807, Sir Davy isolated the element boron from boric acid. However for another century, synthetic chemists found no interest in boron. Around 1910 in Germany, Alfred Stock prepared a series of compounds called boranes, which had high reactivities with many substances.

Around World War II, chemists found boranes could be used for chemical storage of hydrogen for weather balloons and military needs. A popular compound for this purpose was $\ce{NaBH4}$ which reacted with water to give hydrogen.

2.1 The gas obtained by reacting $100\,\mathrm{g}$ of $\ce{NaBH4}$ with water at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ was used to fill a balloon. Write the balanced equation for the reaction of $\ce{NaBH4}$ with water. Assuming the pressure inside the balloon to be approximately equal to outside pressure, estimate the volume of the balloon after the reaction is over. Show the main steps in calculations used to arrive at the answer.

Synthesis method for $\ce{NaBH4}$ was developed by H. C. Brown in USA not to make boranes but to refine uranium. His Ph.D. supervisor Schlesinger had found that uranium forms a volatile complex $\ce{[U(BH4)4]}$ which could be used to separate isotopes of uranium.

2.2 Borohydride anion acts as a ligand in complexes where the metal ion coordinates to the B-H bond and not to any atomic center. Neutron diffraction studies of $\ce{[U(BH4)4]}$ in gas phase show the coordination number of U(IV) to be greater than 8, whereas in solid phase, it exists as a polymeric structure with U(IV) center having coordination number 14. Draw the most stable structures of $\ce{[U(BH4)4]}$ in gaseous and solid phase. You may use dot-wedge notations to represent bonds wherever needed. (Note: steric effects may play a major role here in determining the structures) [Answer box headed: Gas phase; Solid phase.]

Due to developments of other better methods, $\ce{[U(BH4)4]}$ method was eventually not used for uranium refining, but it led to method developments for large scale synthesis of $\ce{NaBH4}$, which became an important reagent in organic synthesis. In 1979, H. C. Brown received the Nobel prize in chemistry for the same.

Another property of boron attracted the attention of nuclear scientists. One of its isotopes, $\ce{^{10}B}$ has a very high affinity to absorb neutrons. Therefore, boron rods could be used as moderators in nuclear reactors to control the fission reaction.

$$\ce{^{10}B + ^{1}n -> [^{11}B] -> ^{4}He + ^{7}Li} + 2.79\,\mathrm{MeV}$$

2.3 The average atomic weight of boron is 10.81 amu and consists of only two isotopes: $\ce{^{10}B}$ and $\ce{^{11}B}$. The masses of these isotopes are 10.0129 amu and 11.0093 amu, respectively. What is the percentage of $\ce{^{10}B}$ atoms in natural Boron samples? Show the steps involved in calculations.

Solutions of boron compounds can also be used to control the number of neutrons (referred as Chemical shims) in nuclear reactors or in case of a nuclear accident.

2.4 Among saturated aqueous solutions of boric acid ($\ce{H3BO3}$) and of borax ($\ce{Na2B4O7.10H2O}$), which will be more effective as chemical shims? Show the calculations needed to arrive at the answer. The solubilities of Boric acid and Borax in water are $52\,\mathrm{g\,L^{-1}}$ and $58\,\mathrm{g\,L^{-1}}$, respectively.

The neutron absorption property of $\ce{^{10}B}$ is also being used for cancer treatment (in Boron Neutron Capture Therapy, BNCT). If one can place a boron-containing molecule inside a cancer cell, then a neutron irradiation will react with boron and the emitted alpha particle can kill selectively the cancer cell, while sparing the normal cells lacking boron. One way of preparing $\ce{^{10}B}$ enriched molecules for BNCT applications is given below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-2-fig1.png

2.4 Identify $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$ & $\mathbf{R}$.

Theoretical explainations of bonding in boranes had always been a challenge. The crystalline form of elemental boron consists of $\ce{B12}$ icosahedra units, each of which in turn is bonded to neighboring icosahedra via boron-boron bonds. A typical structure of icosahedron is given here:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-2-fig2.png

2.5 The maximum number of bonds for a boron atom in this crystalline form of boron is ______

More surprise came when scientists succeeded in preparing similar cage compounds with some of the B atoms replaced with C atoms having the same number of bonds. One such compound is $\ce{C2}$-carborane, whose method of synthesis is indicated below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-2-fig3.png

For BNCT, the tumour cells can be preferentially targeted by attaching a boron-containing molecule to the hormones, as some tumours depend strongly on hormones for growth. In one of the first studies, estrone was used for the purpose, as shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-2-fig4.png

2.6 Draw the structures of $\mathbf{S}$ and $\mathbf{T}$.

2.7 Boron compounds are not only used for therapeutic but also for diagnostic applications. A class of pyrrole-containing boron compounds are used as dyes to stain and image various (transparent) organelles inside the living cells, which are ordinarily difficult to see. The B–N bonds in these compounds are very stable even under biochemical condition, and hence the compounds do not interfere with cellular processes. Two representative examples of such dyes are given below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-2-fig5.png

i. What is the oxidation state of boron in $\mathbf{a}$?

ii. What is the geometry around boron in $\mathbf{a}$?

iii. Out of all three halides (X = F/Cl/Br) in the class of compounds $\mathbf{a}$, which is the most stable species in aqueous conditions?

iv. For a given X (among the stable compounds in aqueous solutions), which dye among $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ will preferentially stain fat tissues?

problems.title: Chemistry behind Henna – Lawsone
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (19 marks). Chemistry behind Henna – Lawsone

Mehendi or henna is known to us as colourant for hands, hair, and fabrics. The orange colour observed from henna is due to a compound called lawsone.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-3-fig1.png

Part I: Properties of Lawsone

Henna leaves, however, do not contain lawsone, but have a class of compounds called hennosides. When the plant cells are ruptured by crushing the leaves, hennosides undergo enzymatic cleavage to generate one equivalent of glucose ($\ce{C6H12O6}$) and a triol $\mathbf{A}$ which on air oxidation produces lawsone. Compound $\mathbf{A}$ also gives a positive test with 2, 4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine.

3.1 Draw structures for the possible hennosides and of the triol $\mathbf{A}$. [Answer box headed: Hennosides; A.]

3.2 Which of the following common substances can promote the hydrolysis of hennoside? (Mark X in the correct box)

• a) Lemon juice
• b) Glucose syrup
• c) $\ce{NaHCO3}$

3.3 Lawsone undergoes tautomerisation in water. Draw the structure of its tautomer $\mathbf{B}$.

Lawsone is yellow in colour at pH below 3.6, above which it undergoes de-protonation in solutions and becomes orange in colour. In strong solutions of alkalies, lawsone undergoes reduction forming a species that is highly stable due to resonance.

3.4 Draw the species obtained by 1 $\ce{e-}$ reduction of deprotonated lawsone. Also draw most stable resonance structures of this reduced species.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-3-fig2.png

Juglone (5-hydroxy derivative of 1,4-naphthalene dione) is a compound structurally similar to lawsone, and occurs in root, leaves, and bark of walnut. Juglone and lawsone, both have intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

3.5 Draw the structures of lawsone and juglone with intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

3.6 Planar molecules would be present in (Mark X in the correct box/es)

• Lawsone
• Juglone

3.7 Out of lawsone and juglone, the compound that is more acidic is (Mark X in the correct box/es)

• Lawsone
• Juglone

Part II: Lawsone in Polymers

Lawsone-based polymers can be used for dyeing of wool and other textiles. A monomer ($\mathbf{C}$) for these polymers was prepared by the following method:

Lawsone ($0.4\,\mathrm{g}$) was dissolved in $10\,\mathrm{mL}$ water-free tetrahydrofuran (THF) under argon gas at room temperature. After $10\,\mathrm{min}$, $0.12\,\mathrm{mL}$ (density = $1.12\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$) 2-propenoyl chloride was added to this solution, followed by the addition of $0.254\,\mathrm{g}$ triethylamine (Mol. Mass = $101.2\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$). A deep red color appeared immediately. The reaction was allowed to undergo completion for $4\,\mathrm{h}$. The solvent was then removed by evaporation. Next, $30\,\mathrm{mL}$ of toluene was added to the mixture, and this solution was shaken with dilute sulfuric acid, and then the aqueous layer was removed. After removing toluene by evaporation, a dark red product ($\mathbf{C}$) was obtained with a yield of 95%.

3.8 Based on the above procedure, give the balanced chemical equation for the reaction leading to formation of $\mathbf{C}$. Also write the reaction conditions (in box above the arrow) necessary for the formation of $\mathbf{C}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-3-fig3.png

3.9 In the above synthesis procedure, triethyl amine acts as a (Mark X in the correct box)

• a) Base
• b) Catalyst
• c) Nucleophile
• d) Acid

3.10 In the above synthesis procedure, which of the reagents is the limiting reagent? Show all the steps in the calculations that help in indicating the limiting reagent.

3.11 Give the reaction involving dilute $\ce{H2SO4}$ taking place when it is shaken with the reaction mixture. Specify the phase in which this reaction occurs.

One student tried this synthesis on a rainy day, and coincidently forgot to attach the Ar gas supply and left the reaction flask open. She could not observe the red product $\mathbf{C}$ in the flask.

3.12 Write the balanced equation for the side reaction due to which the product $\mathbf{C}$ was not formed.

The monomer $\mathbf{C}$ obtained can undergo polymerization in presence of radical initiators.

3.13 Give the structure of the product of the following polymerization reaction of $\mathbf{C}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-3-fig4.png

3.14 For each of the given statements below, mark X in the appropriate box (True / False).

(i) Lawsone and Juglone will have the same physical properties.

(ii) Lawsone can act as an acid-base indicator.

(iii) Lawsone-metal ion system can be used as an oxidizing agent.

problems.title: Gold Refining
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (20 marks). Gold Refining

Even though gold is found in elemental form in nature, separating the element from other minerals found in its ores is a difficult process. Earlier, this separation was achieved by using liquid mercury or chlorine gas. Around 1887, leaching metallic gold in cyanide solution in air was found to be the most effective method which is still used in many parts of the world, including in India.

Part I: Cyanidation Method

This dissolution of gold in NaCN solution is an oxidation-reduction process resulting in a strong complex of cyanide ion with $\ce{Au+}$ ion. This reaction is considered to proceed via two chemical pathways, wherein $\ce{H2O2}$ is formed in one pathway and consumed in the second.

4.1 Write balanced chemical reactions for the two leaching pathways of Au in aqueous $\ce{CN-}$ solution in presence of air leading to the formation of the gold complex.

Solubility of $\ce{O2}$ in water at room temperature and 1 atm pressure is very low ($8.2\,\mathrm{mg\,L^{-1}}$). Interestingly, this process is economical even with this concentration of oxygen. Therefore, cyanide concentrations used for effective leaching are also not very high.

4.2 Assuming that the leaching reactions proceed to completion faster than the diffusion of atmospheric $\ce{O2}$ in water, what minimum concentration of NaCN (in $\mathrm{g\,L^{-1}}$) is desirable for maximum gold leaching at room temperature and 1 atm?

4.3 Write the most preferable geometry and spin magnetic moment ($\mu_\text{spin only}$) value of the gold cyanide complex formed.

The reduction potential for $\ce{Au+(aq)}$ ion ($E^\circ_{\ce{Au+}/\ce{Au}} = +1.69\,\mathrm{V}$) is much higher than that of $\ce{O2}$, indicating that gold is stable with respect to oxidation by oxygen at all pH values. Presence of strong complexing agents such as $\ce{CN-}$, which can stabilize gold in either +1 or +3 oxidation states, significantly shifts the reduction potential of gold. Cyanide ions affect the equilibria of the reaction $\ce{Au+(aq) + e- <=> Au(s)}$ due to the following additional equilibrium:

$$\ce{[Au(CN)2]-(aq) <=> Au+(aq) + 2CN-(aq)} \qquad \mathrm{p}K = 38.3 \ (\text{at } 25\,^\circ\mathrm{C})$$

4.4 Find the $E^\circ$ value for the following half-cell reaction and write its Nernst equation.

$$\ce{[Au(CN)2]-(aq) + e- <=> Au(s) + 2CN-(aq)}$$

Electrochemical potentials of several redox systems change with pH. This dependence is graphically represented in form of the $E_\mathrm{H}$ (potential) vs pH diagrams. The reduction potential $E_\mathrm{H}$ of a half-cell reaction relative to Standard Hydrogen Electrode is plotted on the y-axis with pH on the x-axis. Regions on different sides of plotted lines indicate domains of E and pH values at which specific species will be predominant (due to thermodynamic stability) under equilibrium conditions. These diagrams are based on the Nernst equation (based only on thermodynamics), but give no information about the reaction kinetics.

The $E_\mathrm{H}$ vs pH diagrams of (a) Au, (b) Ag, (c) Pd and (d) Pt in 0.02 M NaCN solution at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ are shown below. The $\ce{H2O}$ stability limits are represented by the two dotted lines which correspond to the equilibria:

$$\ce{O2(g) + 4H+(aq) + 4e- <=> 2H2O(aq)}$$

$$\ce{2H+(aq) + 2e- <=> H2(g)}$$

Regions $\mathbf{1}$ and $\mathbf{2}$ represent stability domains for $\ce{O2}$ and $\ce{H2}$ (both at unit activity), respectively.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-4-fig1.png

4.5 Based on the information given in above diagrams for Au, Ag, Pd, and Pt at pH = 7,

(i) identify the metals which can be leached out using NaCN solution in presence of $\ce{O2}$.

(ii) arrange the leachable metals identified in (i) in descending order of ease of leaching using the above cyanidation process at the given pH.

4.6 The most suitable pH for Au extraction using NaCN solution in presence of $\ce{O2}$ is ______

Many gold ores also contain copper minerals. Thus, during cyanidation, some copper minerals readily dissolve forming several copper(I)-cyanide complexes. These can reduce the process efficiency (and economics) due to high cyanide consumption, leading to reduced gold leach rates and poor gold recovery.

The pH dependency of the speciation of copper (I) cyanide complexes is shown in the following plot, where $a_\mathrm{i}$ is the ratio between concentrations of a cyanide complex and of total dissolved copper.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-4-fig2.png

4.7 Write the formulae of copper(I) cyano complexes most likely to be extracted along with Au during the cyanidation process at the most suitable pH condition (identified in 4.6 above).

To separate the dissolved gold complexes from dissolved copper complexes, activated carbon is added to the leached solution. The Au(I) cyanide complex ions preferentially move into the pores of activated carbon compared to the Cu(I) cyanide complex.

4.8 Mark the correct reason/s for the above observation from the following options (Mark X in the correct box/es)

• (a) Lower hydration of Au(I) cyanide complex anion.
• (b) Lower hydration of Cu(I) cyanide complex anion.
• (c) Higher charge density of Au(I) cyanide complex anion.
• (d) Higher charge density of Cu(I) cyanide complex anion.

The gold complexes are then removed from activated carbon by elution with a NaOH/NaCN solution, from which gold is recovered by electrowinning.

Part II: Thiourea Method

The use of thiourea, $\ce{NH2CSNH2}$, as an extracting agent for precious metals like gold has shown promise as it is less toxic compared to the reagents used in the cyanidation process.

4.9 Write the balanced chemical equation for reaction of Au with thiourea in presence of ferric ion (which is used as an oxidant) leading to the formation of the gold complex.

One of the factors that prevents the economic viability of thiourea use in gold leaching is the irreversible loss of thiourea by oxidation.

4.10 Write the structure of the product formed by oxidation of thiourea in presence of ferric ions in the following (balanced) reaction.

$$\ce{2CS(NH2)2} + \ce{2Fe^{3+}} \longrightarrow \boxed{\phantom{XXXXXX}} + \ce{2H+} + \ce{2Fe^{2+}}$$

When thiourea is separately mixed with $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ solution, the oxidation reaction was found to be second-order reaction with a rate constant of $1.55\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}\,s^{-1}}$ at $303\,\mathrm{K}$. The activation energy for the process was found to be $79\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$.

For the leaching reaction of Au by thiourea and $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$, activation energy is $8.5\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$.

4.11 Determine the ratios of the rate constants at temperature $303\,\mathrm{K}$ to $295\,\mathrm{K}$ for the leaching and the thiourea oxidation reactions. Based on the ratios, deduce whether Au recovery per kg of thiourea will be more at $295\,\mathrm{K}$ or at $303\,\mathrm{K}$ under identical conditions? Show steps to arrive at the answers.

The Au-thiourea complex is separated from the leaching solution using ion-exchange resins. Ion exchange resins are polymeric compounds having side groups, with which some of the ions in the solution can bind or can exchange for an ion associated with the resin.

4.12 Of the following, the ion-exchange resin(s) that will lead to adsorption of Au-thiourea complex are (Mark X in the correct box/es)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-4-fig3.png

The Au-thiourea complex is extracted from the ion exchange resin into a solution and then pure gold is obtained by electrowinning of this solution. In this process, current is passed through an inert anode, the metal is deposited onto the cathode and thiourea remains in the electrolyte. The amount of thiourea is determined by titrating with $\ce{KIO3}$ solution in the presence of starch indicator.

4.13 Thiourea is oxidized by potassium iodate in acid solution and forms $\ce{[CS(NH2)2]2^{2+}}$. Write down the balanced equation for the associated reaction.

4.14 Standard $\ce{KIO3}$ solution was prepared by dissolving $5.35\,\mathrm{g}$ of $\ce{KIO3}$ in 1 litre of distilled water. $50.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of thiourea sample (after electrowinning) was taken in a beaker. Few mL of $\ce{H3PO4}$ solution and 4-5 drops of starch indicator was added to it and the mixture was titrated using $\ce{KIO3}$ solution. The equivalence point was observed after addition of $20.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of $\ce{KIO3}$ solution. Calculate the amount of gold (in g) recovered from 1 L of the Au-thiourea complex solution that was used for electrowinning.

problems.title: Phosphate and Struvite
problems.problem:
Problem 5 (24 marks). Phosphate and Struvite

Part I: Struvite from Phosphate

Phosphorus is an essential element in living organisms, critical for bones and biomolecules like glyophosphates, DNA, RNA, ATP, etc. For plants also, phosphorus fertilizers are considered important (among NPK fertilizers) – the most common being the orthophosphate salts.

On the other hand, high concentrations of phosphates in rivers and lakes is a serious environmental concern as these cause toxic algal blooms, 'dead zones' and health hazards. Important sources of phosphorus in water bodies include sewage discharges and run-offs from agricultural fields. Since phosphorus is mostly present in wastewaters as phosphates, one of the parameters defining the performance of a sewage treatment plant is the phosphate reduction in the wastewater during the treatment.

Concentration of phosphorus (as phosphates) in a solution can be estimated by adding $\ce{MgSO4}$ and $\ce{NH3}$. Mass of the resulting precipitate $\ce{MgNH4PO4.6H2O}$ i.e. magnesium ammonium phosphate hexahydrate (MAP, also known as struvite) indicates the concentration of phosphorus in the sample.

5.1 If $100\,\mathrm{mL}$ of a standard phosphate salt solution yields $10.496\,\mathrm{mg}$ of MAP precipitate after addition of excess of $\ce{MgSO4}$ and $\ce{NH3}$, calculate the phosphorus content (in $\mathrm{mg\,L^{-1}}$) of the sample.

5.2 Phosphorus content in a wastewater sample was determined by the MAP method as well as a standard spectroscopic method. The estimated phosphorus content by the MAP method had an error of 2%. The error in a measurement is defined as

$$\text{Error} = |\text{Measured value} - \text{Actual Value}| \,/\, \text{Actual Value}$$

Chemical analysis of the precipitate showed that the molar ratio of $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$:$\ce{NH4+}$:$\ce{PO4^{3-}}$ deviated from 1:1:1. Further the precipitate also had some $\ce{MgKPO4.6H2O}$ (MKP), due to high $\ce{K+}$ concentration in the wastewater which could explain the 2% error. What is the molar ratio of MAP:MKP in the precipitate?

5.3 On heating, a pure sample of MAP undergoes change in mass due to gradual loss of volatile components. The mass percentage of solid remaining at each temperature is given as follows:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-5-fig1.png

The figures in the brackets indicate the approximate % mass loss at $205\,\mathrm{K}$ and $315\,\mathrm{K}$, respectively. The solid at $205\,\mathrm{K}$ is a single compound $\mathbf{A}$, whereas at $315\,\mathrm{K}$ is a mixture of $\mathbf{A}$ and another compound $\mathbf{B}$ in approximately equal mass ratio. Identify $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$, and their molar masses. Show steps needed to arrive at answer.

Part II: Precipitation Conditions for Struvite

Sewage often contains $\ce{NH4+}$ and $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$ ions along with phosphates in appreciable concentrations. Thus, struvite precipitation is common in sewage, causing blockage in pipes. Precipitation of struvite from a solution, however, highly depends on the pH, as several ionic equilibria affect its dissolution equilibrium. To understand the precipitation conditions for struvite, we shall first try to understand some of the equilibria involved. Consider an element that can exist in form of multiple species $\mathrm{X_1}, \ldots, \mathrm{X_n}$ in a system. The relative percentage of the specie $\mathrm{X_n}$ is given as

$$\%\mathrm{X_n} = \frac{[\mathrm{X_n}]}{\sum_n [\mathrm{X_n}]} \times 100$$

For example, phosphate can exist as $\ce{PO4^{3-}}$, $\ce{HPO4^{2-}}$, $\ce{H2PO4-}$, and $\ce{H3PO4}$ in solutions depending on the pH.

5.4 Given that $\ce{H3PO4}$ has $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a1} = 2.30$, $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a2} = 7.20$, and $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a3} = 12.32$, estimate the relative ratios $[\ce{PO4^{3-}}] : [\ce{H2PO4-}]$ at pH = 7, and $[\ce{PO4^{3-}}] : [\ce{HPO4^{2-}}]$ at pH = 11.

Another relevant pH-dependent process is the equilibrium between ammonium ions and ammonia

$$\ce{NH4+(aq) <=> NH3(aq) + H+(aq)} \qquad \mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = 9.24$$

5.5 Assuming no ammonia escapes from the solution at any time, plot a graph of % $\ce{NH4+}$ as a function of pH, by determining the required coordinates corresponding to the following three points

a) pH = $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}$ (point $\mathbf{Z_1}$)

b) pH = 11.0 (point $\mathbf{Z_2}$)

c) pH where % $\ce{NH4+}$ ~ 99% (point $\mathbf{Z_3}$)

Show calculations for the coordinates of the three points. Also, label the three points on the curve.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-5-fig2.png

5.6 Depending on the pH of the solution, $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$ ions may hydrolyze to water soluble $\ce{MgOH+}$ species or precipitate as $\ce{Mg(OH)2}$.

$$\ce{Mg(OH)2(s) <=> Mg^{2+}(aq) + 2OH-(aq)} \qquad K_\mathrm{sp} = 5.61\times10^{-12}$$

$$\ce{Mg^{2+}(aq) + OH-(aq) <=> MgOH+(aq)} \qquad K_1 = 3.98\times10^{2}$$

Consider a solution of 0.002 M $\ce{MgCl2}$ prepared in a buffer of pH = 11. Determine % $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$ (relative to all soluble Mg species) in this solution. Show the steps involved.

Precipitation of struvite at any given pH will take place only if the ionic product (I.P., product of concentrations of the three ions) exceeds its solubility product ($K_\mathrm{sp}$ of struvite = $5.0\times10^{-12}$).

$$\text{I. P.} = [\ce{Mg^{2+}}][\ce{NH4+}][\ce{PO4^{3-}}]$$

5.7 Suppose a sewage water sample contains 2 mM total dissolved $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$, 30 mM total dissolved $\ce{NH3}$ and 3 mM total soluble phosphate at pH = 7.

(i) Determine the I. P. values at pH = 7 and pH = 11. Assume no other ionic equibria exists involving the three ions, other than those mentioned in this problem. Assume the temperature to be same for all calculations.

(ii) In the graph below, plot log (I.P.) values for pH = 7 and pH = 11 based on your calculations in 5.7 (i). Two points corresponding to pH = 8.5 and 9.5 are given here. Plot the dependence of log (I.P.) vs pH based on the four points and thus, deduce the pH range in which struvite will precipitate under equilibrium conditions. Assume the temperature to be same for all calculations.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-5-fig3.png

pH Range: ______

5.8 The dissolution of struvite has a peculiarity that it is endothermic at lower temperature and exothermic above a certain temperature. Which of the following graph/s qualitatively indicates this property of struvite (mark X in the correct box/es)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2019-5-fig4.png

Controlled precipitation of struvite in sewage treatment plants is being used in some countries to recover valuable phosphorus for use as a slow-release fertilizer. In this approach, the sewage water (usually at pH ~ 7.0) is retained in a reactor and subject to conditions which promote struvite precipitation. The struvite precipitation in reaction reduces the phosphorus content in the effluent as well as the precipitation and clogging in pipes.

5.9 Given below are four interventions possible in the sewage tank. State the effect of each of these on the struvite precipitation (Write the statement number i-iv, as applicable for each option)

• (i) no effect
• (ii) increase in precipitation
• (iii) decrease in precipitation

problems.title: Chemistry of the artificial hair dyes
problems.problem:
Problem 1 (16 marks). Chemistry of the artificial hair dyes

Dyeing of hair is an ancient art. Earlier, dyes were obtained from plants such as indigo, henna, turmeric and amla. In dyeing with natural henna, an aglycone molecule (structure shown below), gets converted to orange colored Lawsone in the presence of an oxidant (such as air).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-1-fig1.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-1-fig2.png

Hydroquinone (1,4-dihydroxybenzene) and analogous 1,4-diimine derivatives also undergo similar transformations under the influence of an oxidant.

A chemistry teacher at a hair salon once observed the barber preparing a low-cost hair colorant for a customer by mixing a spoonful of brownish-white crystalline solid with $\ce{H2O2}$ and shaving cream. A little investigation indicated that the white solid was a chemical called PPD (p-phenylenediamine).

On further reading, the teacher realized that PPD was one of the first synthetic chemical launched for hair dyeing market in the year 1907. Later he found that most of the hair colorants being sold in the market, including the so-called "natural/herbal" hair colours had PPD in them. Hair proteins have iso-ionic points (when the number of +ve and –ve charged species in protein are equal) around pH = 4.8–6.8. Therefore, some of the hair dyes are also +vely charged species, which hair proteins absorb from neutral-alkaline solutions.

In this problem, we will explore how colourless PPD leads to the intense black and numerous other hair colours.

Under oxidizing condition, PPD gets converted to corresponding diimine $\mathbf{A}$ ($\ce{C6H6N2}$).

1.1 Draw the structure of $\mathbf{A}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-1-fig3.png

In aqueous solutions in the pH range 7-10, a small fraction of $\mathbf{A}$ molecules exists in monoprotonated form $\mathbf{B}$.

1.2 Draw the structure of $\mathbf{B}$.

Usually colour in organic molecules originates due to extended conjugation. Black colour is generated from PPD by two pathways $\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{II}$.

Pathway I: In many commercial hair colorants, the white powder contains a mixture of several compounds (called couplers) along with PPD. Under oxidizing conditions, PPD reacts with different couplers producing different hair colors, which in specific combination give black colour.

For example, oxidized form of PPD ($\mathbf{B}$) reacts with the coupler m-phenylenediamine in aqueous phase to form the thermodynamically stable product $\mathbf{C}$, which on further oxidation produces a blue hair dye $\mathbf{D}$ (a cationic species having two rings).

1.3 Write the structure of $\mathbf{C}$ and dye $\mathbf{D}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-1-fig4.png

When resorcinol is used as a coupler, a yellow-green dye $\mathbf{E}$ is produced which reacts with diazomethane to form a compound having molecular formula $\ce{C20H18N4O2}$.

1.4 Write the structure of $\mathbf{E}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-1-fig5.png

Pathway II: When PPD is alone subjected to oxidation, the oxidized form $\mathbf{A}$ slowly gets polymerized to give an intermediate $\mathbf{F}$, which on further oxidation gives an intense black hair colour.

1.5 Write the part-structure of the polymer ($\mathbf{F}$).

The oxidative coupling of 4-dimethylamino aniline with phenol can take a different pathway. A $2\,e^-$ oxidation of 4-dimethylamino aniline generates a cationic intermediate species $\mathbf{G}$. Reaction of phenol with $\mathbf{G}$, produces a colourless species leuco-indoaniline, which gets easily oxidized to give a dye, indoaniline.

Quantum mechanical calculations indicate that conversion from $\mathbf{G}$ to leuco-indoaniline can go through a very low energy pathway involving formation of another intermediate species $\mathbf{H}$. Due to $\pi$-$\pi$ stacking interactions between two rings, $\mathbf{H}$ can easily rearrange to produce leuco-indoaniline.

1.6 Draw the most stable resonance form of $\mathbf{G}$ and possible structure of $\mathbf{H}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-1-fig6.png

Around the period of discovery of poly-PPD, scientists were able to polymerize aniline also. Some poly-anilines were found to be good electrical conductors, leading to Nobel Prize award in 2000 to Alan G. MacDiarmid, Alan J. Heeger and Hideki Shirakawa. In acidic medium and presence of an oxidant, aniline first forms a polymer $\mathbf{I}$ having empirical formula $\ce{C12H10N2}$, which on subsequent partial oxidation (with 50% of the polymer chain getting oxidized) produces $\mathbf{J}$. Protonated form of $\mathbf{J}$ exhibits high electrical conductivity.

1.7 Write the part structures of polymers $\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{J}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-1-fig7.png

A particular brand of hair colour (labelled "herbal black henna") contains the following ingredients: barium peroxide, citric acid, magnesium carbonate, and PPD, along with some herbs (Amla, Neem leaves, Shikakai, Coffee seeds, Tulsi, etc.) which don't participate in the colour forming reactions. Application of its paste with water makes the hair black. A paste of natural henna leaves is also applied to hair for giving orange colour.

1.8 When a paste of henna leaves was mixed (in 1:1 ratio) with the "herbal black henna", black colour was not produced in significant intensity. Write the chemical reaction that took place and prevented formation of black colour.

PPD based hair dyes can lead to skin allergies and related diseases. Hence, researchers are trying for new hair dyes. Efforts have been made to prepare hair colours using 4-(N,N-dimethylamino) benzaldehyde.

The reaction of 3-ethyl-2-methylbenzothiazolium iodide ($\mathbf{K}$) with 4-(N,N-dimethylamino) benzaldehyde ($\mathbf{L}$) in presence of a base gives an intensely coloured dye $\mathbf{N}$, which has the longest possible conjugation of $\pi$-bonds.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-1-fig8.png

The reaction proceeds through the formation of intermediate $\mathbf{M}$ (obtained from reaction of $\mathbf{K}$ with base).

1.9 Draw the possible structure(s) of the intermediate $\mathbf{M}$ and the dye(s) $\mathbf{N}$.

problems.title: Towards a new Metallurgy from e-waste
problems.problem:
Problem 2 (22 marks). Towards a new Metallurgy from e-waste

The global market for electrical and electronic equipment continues to expand, while the lifespan of products is becoming shorter. A large amount of metals mined from earth crust are now being piled up in heaps of electronic waste (e-waste). With many of the natural metal ores being exhausted, there is a need to develop chemistry to extract metals and their compounds from e-waste.

One of the most complex components in e-waste are Printed Circuit boards (PCBs). The average metallic composition of a typical PCB from a computer is 20.1% Cu, 7.2% Fe, 3.6% Al, 2.8% Zn, 2.1% Pb, 3.3% Sn, and 0.7% Ni. Apart from these, Ag or some other metals are also present in some e-waste depending on the design of the electronic components.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-2-fig1.png

Consider a sample of PCB waste that contains all the above mentioned 8 metals including Ag. To extract metals, e-waste is first grinded to a powder form and then subjected to separation processes. Pieces of metallic Fe and Al, present in component casing, etc, are separated by magnetic separation and Eddy current technique, respectively. Note that these physical methods may only separate the elemental forms and not compounds or alloys of Fe and Al.

Chemical processing of the ground powder starts by dissolving in concentrated nitric acid. The reaction of metals with nitric acid varies greatly depending on the metal, its form and the concentration of the acid.

2.1 A common reaction product is NO gas. List the other possible N-containing molecules/ions that can result from reactions of nitric acid with metals.

2.2 An important task for the recycler is to know the amount of $\ce{HNO3}$ solution required for complete dissolution of the metals present in an e-waste powder. Which of the following information would be necessary to know the minimum required amount of nitric acid? (Mark X in the box (es))

a) Stoichiometric ratio of metals and their compounds and nitric acid in their reactions
b) Mass percentages of various metals and their compounds present in the ground e-waste
c) Density of pure metals and their compounds present in e-waste
d) Atomic masses of various metals present
e) Concentration of nitric acid
f) $\Delta H$ of the reactions representing formation of metal nitrates

2.3 If metallic copper reacts with $1\,\mathrm{M}$ $\ce{HNO3}$, NO gas is produced.
a) Write the individual oxidation and reduction reactions indicating the electron transfer and the balanced equation for the overall reaction.
b) Calculate the minimum volume of $1\,\mathrm{M}$ $\ce{HNO3}$ required to completely dissolve $100\,\mathrm{g}$ of Cu.

In the following part, we are presenting a model procedure for separation of the components from ground PCB.

2.4 Treatment of ground PCB powder with concentrated $\ce{HNO3}$ produces a white precipitate $\mathbf{P_1}$. A major fraction of $\mathbf{P_1}$ is due to a metal $\mathbf{Y}$, which is one of the major components of solder, reacting with the acid and forming the hydrated form of its oxide liberating a brown gas. Identify $\mathbf{Y}$ and write the balanced chemical equation of this reaction.

The filtrate $\mathbf{F_1}$ obtained after removing $\mathbf{P_1}$ from the mixture is then mixed with dil. HCl and filtered to obtain a precipitate $\mathbf{P_2}$ and a filtrate $\mathbf{F_2}$. $\mathbf{P_2}$ is boiled with water for few minutes and filtered while hot to obtain filtrate $\mathbf{F_3}$. To a small portion of $\mathbf{F_3}$, addition of $\ce{K2CrO4}$ yields a yellow precipitate, $\mathbf{P_3}$.

2.5 Identify the composition of $\mathbf{P_2}$ and $\mathbf{P_3}$.

From the filtrate $\mathbf{F_2}$, metals $\mathbf{M_1}$ (which was present in $\mathbf{P_2}$ but has not completely precipitated in the previous step) and $\mathbf{M_2}$ are precipitated out by passing $\ce{H2S}$ gas through the solution, which on filtration, gives a precipitate $\mathbf{P_4}$ and filtrate $\mathbf{F_4}$.

Apart from $\mathbf{M_1}$ and $\mathbf{M_2}$, there are two more metals $\mathbf{M_3}$ and $\mathbf{M_4}$ in $\mathbf{F_2}$ that can be precipitated with $\ce{H2S}$. However, the precipitation of these is governed by the pH of the solution. $K_{sp}$ values of the sulphides of these metals are: $\mathbf{M_1}$: $1\times10^{-28}$; $\mathbf{M_2}$: $1\times10^{-37}$; $\mathbf{M_3}$: $1\times10^{-22}$; $\mathbf{M_4}$: $1\times10^{-23}$

2.6 Determine the minimum $[\ce{H+}]$ required to separate $\mathbf{M_1}$ and $\mathbf{M_2}$ from $\mathbf{M_3}$ and $\mathbf{M_4}$ by passing $\ce{H2S}$ through the solution. (Assume that the precipitation is complete when the concentration of precipitated metal ion reduces to $10^{-6}\,\mathrm{M}$ and the saturated concentration of $\ce{H2S}$ in water as well as in acidic solutions is $3.8\,\mathrm{g\,L^{-1}}$. $\mathbf{M_1}$, $\mathbf{M_2}$, $\mathbf{M_3}$ and $\mathbf{M_4}$ are divalent in nature). Show all steps of calculations. For $\ce{H2S}$, $K_{a1} = 1.0\times10^{-7}$, $K_{a2} = 1.0\times10^{-19}$.

The precipitate $\mathbf{P_4}$ is re-dissolved in $6\,\mathrm{M}$ $\ce{HNO3}$ and mixed with concentrated $\ce{H2SO4}$ and boiled. $\mathbf{M_1}$ precipitates then as $\mathbf{P_5}$ and a filtrate $\mathbf{F_5}$ is obtained. On passing $\ce{H2S}$ gas through filtrate $\mathbf{F_5}$, a black precipitate $\mathbf{P_6}$ is obtained.

2.7 Identify the composition of $\mathbf{P_5}$ and $\mathbf{P_6}$.

The filtrate $\mathbf{F_4}$ is boiled well in air to expel a gas and then $\ce{NH4Cl}$ is added followed by excess of $\ce{NH4OH}$. During this process $\mathbf{M_5}$ and $\mathbf{M_6}$ gets precipitated as $\mathbf{P_7}$, which after filtration leaves filtrate, $\mathbf{F_6}$. The precipitate $\mathbf{P_7}$ after washing with water is relatively safe for disposing in soil (as its components are found in many natural soils).

2.8 Identify which gas was necessary to be expelled by boiling and the composition of precipitate $\mathbf{P_7}$.

2.9 If excess $\ce{NH4OH}$ is added before adding $\ce{NH4Cl}$, then two other metals $\mathbf{M_3}$ and $\mathbf{M_4}$ also get precipitated. Write the chemical reactions for precipitations for these metals.

2.10 Determine the pH of a solution prepared by adding $50\,\mathrm{g}$ of $\ce{NH4Cl}$ to $100\,\mathrm{mL}$ water followed by addition of $100\,\mathrm{mL}$ solution of $1\,\mathrm{M}$ $\ce{NH4OH}$. ($K_{b\,(\ce{NH4OH})} = 1.8\times10^{-5}$)

The filtrate $\mathbf{F_6}$ is saturated with $\ce{H2S}$ to obtain $\mathbf{M_3}$ and $\mathbf{M_4}$ as precipitate $\mathbf{P_8}$. The precipitate $\mathbf{P_8}$ on treating with dilute HCl leads to dissolution of precipitate $\mathbf{M_4}$ only that is separated as filtrate $\mathbf{F_7}$. The filtrate is neutralized using aqueous NaOH solution and on passing $\ce{H2S}$ again through the filtrate dirty white precipitate $\mathbf{P_9}$ is obtained.

2.11 Identify precipitates of $\mathbf{M_3}$ and $\mathbf{M_4}$ in $\mathbf{P_8}$.

2.12 Which of the following reagents used above is not essential for the separation of metals from e-waste in the method presented above: $\ce{HNO3}$, HCl, $\ce{NH4Cl}$, $\ce{NH4OH}$, $\ce{H2S}$, $\ce{K2CrO4}$, NaOH.

problems.title: Growth Hormones for Apples
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (24 marks). Growth Hormones for Apples

The red colour of the peel is a key quality marker for many varieties of apples, which affects consumer preferences for the fruit in market. Several chemicals are used at different stages of apple growth to modify anthocyanin content of the fruit and hence its colour.

Ethephon (structure given) is a major agrochemical used in India which promotes fruit maturity, increases the red skin color and allows early harvest of apples. One of the routes to prepare Ethephon is by using phosphorus trichloride and 1,2-epoxyethane to give a phosphite $\mathbf{A}$ ($\ce{C6H12Cl3O3P}$). $\mathbf{A}$ undergoes rearrangement to a phosphonate $\mathbf{B}$ which hydrolyses to yield Ethephon.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-3-fig1.png

3.1 Give the structures of $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$.

3.2 Using the data of bond energies given below and by showing appropriate calculations, determine if the rearrangement $\mathbf{A} \rightarrow \mathbf{B}$ will lead to heating or cooling of the reaction mixture.

$$\begin{array}{l|l|l|l} \text{Bonds} & \text{Bond dissociation energy } (\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}) & \text{Bonds} & \text{Bond dissociation energy } (\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}) \\ \hline \text{P–O} & 335 & \text{C–O} & 358 \\ \text{P=O} & 544 & \text{C–P} & 264 \\ \text{C–C} & 348 & \text{C–Cl} & 338 \end{array}$$

Commercially, Ethephon is sold in about $360\,\mathrm{g\,L^{-1}}$ aqueous solutions.

3.3 Determine the pH of the above Ethephon solution. For Ethephon, $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a1} = 2.82$, $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a2} = 7.21$.

In aqueous solutions with pH > 5, Ethephon undergoes slow decomposition via two different pathways to give different products.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-3-fig2.png

In pathway I, one of the decomposition products $\mathbf{C}$ is a natural plant hormone. $\mathbf{C}$ is a colourless gas at room temperature which if treated with bromine followed by treatment with $\ce{NaNH2}$ in liquid ammonia gives a colourless gas $\mathbf{D}$.

In Pathway II, one of the decomposition products is a carbon containing compound $\mathbf{E}$, which is toxic for liver in animals. Pure $\mathbf{E}$ is a viscous oily liquid at room temperature.

3.4 Draw the structures of $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{D}$, and $\mathbf{E}$.

A $0.04\,\mathrm{M}$ solution of Ethephon was prepared in aqueous NaOH. The solution had a pH = 7.5 at time $t = 0\,\mathrm{s}$. The volume of gas $\mathbf{C}$ evolved ($V_t$) from this solution was monitored as a function of time $t$ at $30\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The data obtained is presented in the graph below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-3-fig3.png

3.5 Using the data in the above graph, calculate the rate constant of the decomposition pathway I.

Ethephon solutions for farm applications are prepared usually in carrier water (dilute solutions of sodium or calcium carbonate), which generates solutions with pH of about 7-8.

3.6 A farmer took a $200\,\mathrm{mL}$ bottle of $360\,\mathrm{g\,L^{-1}}$ Ethephon and diluted the content in carrier water at $30\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to obtain $200\,\mathrm{L}$ solution at 12:30 pm. After that he went for lunch and started spraying this solution on plants at 2:30 pm. If decomposition by pathway I was predominant during this time, by what fraction did the concentration of Ethephon drop in the spray solution due to lunch break by the farmer?

Due to toxic effects of Ethephon by-products, there has been constant search for other plant growth regulators. Another such hormone being used is methyl jasmonate extracted from jasmine flower. It also promotes ripening, enhances the red color, and decreases the chlorophyll content in the apples. One of the routes to synthesize methyl jasmonate is detailed below.

The first step involves a reaction of the following diester with a base to yield a cyclic product $\mathbf{P}$. $\mathbf{P}$ on isolation and subsequent reaction with the given alkyl halide gives the compound $\mathbf{Q}$, following the reaction sequence given below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-3-fig4.png

3.7 Draw the structures of $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$.

3.8 The formation of $\mathbf{P}$ will be favoured if the solution of starting material is (Mark X in the correct box)
i) concentrated
ii) dilute

3.9 The most suitable solvent for conversion of $\mathbf{P}$ to $\mathbf{Q}$ is (Mark X in the correct box)
(i) N,N-dimethyl formamide
(ii) ethanol
(iii) n-hexane

3.10 $\mathbf{Q}$ on treatment with palladium acetate and triphenyl phosphine yields a compound $\mathbf{R}$ and, among other products, a gas which turns lime water milky. Draw the structure of $\mathbf{R}$.

$\mathbf{R}$ is then converted to $\mathbf{S}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-3-fig5.png

3.11 The best reagent for converting $\mathbf{R}$ to $\mathbf{S}$ is (Mark X in the appropriate box)
a) $\ce{H2}$ / 5% Pd - $\ce{CaCO3}$
b) $\ce{Na}$/$\ce{C2H5OH}$ + $\ce{NH3}$
c) $\ce{LiAlH4}$ / $\ce{AlCl3}$
d) conc $\ce{H2SO4}$
e) NaOH/$\ce{H2O}$/ Heat
f) Pyridinium Chlorochromate/$\ce{Al2O3}$/Hexane

3.12 $\mathbf{T}$ is the other stereoisomer of $\mathbf{S}$. Draw the structure of $\mathbf{T}$.

3.13 $\mathbf{S}$ on treatment with the dimethyl malonate in sodium methoxide and methanol gives the addition product $\mathbf{U}$. Draw the structure of $\mathbf{U}$?

3.14 $\mathbf{U}$ is then mixed with 1 equivalent of adipic acid and heated at $190\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ for 6 hours. At the end, excess aqueous $\ce{NaHCO3}$ is added to the flask and shaken well. Then the aqueous portion is removed leaving behind a liquid in the flask from which the methyl jasmonate is obtained by distillation. The aqueous solution on evaporation gives sodium monomethyl adipate and $\ce{NaHCO3}$. Draw the structure of methyl jasmonate.

3.15 Write the number of the optical stereoisomers of methyl jasmonate (such that the configuration at the unsaturated bond is same as that in $\mathbf{S}$).

problems.title: Water and Heat
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (13 marks). Water and Heat

In this problem, we will try to estimate the impact of evaporation on temperature changes in a kitchen. Usually an important parameter related to air temperature is its relative humidity, which can be defined as

$$\text{Relative humidity} = \frac{\text{Amount of water vapour per unit volume of air}}{\text{Saturation vapour content per unit volume of air at that temperature}}.$$

Saturation vapour content of air $m_\mathrm{sat}$ (in g per $\mathrm{m^3}$ of air) is a function of air temperature and is given by:

$$m_\mathrm{sat} = 22 + 0.72\,(T - 298)$$

where $T$ is the air temperature in K.

A kitchen has an air volume of $12.1\,\mathrm{m^3}$ and a LPG (predominantly butane) cylinder based stove. Consider the kitchen a closed system and assume kitchen walls, door and window as adiabatic. On a day, the kitchen air had a relative humidity of 13.0%, temperature of $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and a pressure of 1 atm. In a steel vessel (heat capacity: $110\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$), $1.800\,\mathrm{kg}$ of water was kept on flame for heating. When the water just started boiling, the gas flame was turned off. During this process, the mass of gas cylinder decreased by $15.2\,\mathrm{g}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-4-fig1.png

When the temperature of water is changing (during heating or cooling), the amount of water that evaporates at any given temperature is variable. For simplicity, in this situation assume that whatever water evaporates in a process, it evaporates at the middle temperature of the starting and the final temperatures of that process.

Assume the following quantities to be constant over the temperature range involved in this problem.
1) Calorific value of butane = $49.1\,\mathrm{kJ\,g^{-1}}$
2) Specific Heat of Water = $4.18\,\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$
3) Latent Heat of Evaporation of water = $42.20\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
4) For air (assuming to be ideal diatomic gas), $C_\mathrm{p} = 5R/2$; $C_\mathrm{v} = 7R/2$, where $R$ is the universal gas constant

4.1 Consider Stage 1 to be the period of heating of water till the flame was just turned off. Assume that during this stage, there was negligible change in temperature and pressure of the kitchen air. Determine the increase in relative humidity of the air at the end of this stage, if all the heat released from flame was absorbed by the water-vessel system.

If you could not determine the increase in relative humidity in above question, take this value to be 50% for further questions in this problem.

4.2 Consider Stage 2 to be the period after the flame was just turned off. During this stage, the water starts cooling, which leads to heating of air. Determine the kitchen air temperature in K when the system reaches thermal equilibrium under the following two possibilities. Note: Starting point of both these possibilities is the end of Stage 1 (defined in 4.1).

Possibility a) After switching off the flame, the water surface in the vessel was covered with a thin lid of negligible heat capacity and there was negligible air space in the container (thus assume no water evaporated during this phase).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-4-fig2.png

Possibility b) If the vessel was kept open during cooling stage (hence, the water could evaporate).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-4-fig3.png

This problem shows that how important evaporation from hot foods is in controlling heating of surrounding air particularly in absence of air circulation.

problems.title: The different forms of Solid CaCO3
problems.problem:
Problem 5 (29 marks). The different forms of Solid $\ce{CaCO3}$

$\ce{CaCO3}$ is one of the most common minerals in living & non-living natural world. In industries, it deposits in many systems due to presence of $\ce{Ca^{2+}}$ in waters and $\ce{CO2}$ in air. In all these systems, $\ce{CaCO3}$ is found in 6 different forms: one amorphous form, two hydrated crystalline forms and three anhydrous crystalline forms (Calcite, Aragonite and Vaterite) with different physico-chemical properties. Formation and dissolution conditions of these forms are very important to understand while dealing with these systems.

At STP, calcite is thermodynamically the most stable form. Calcite crystallizes in hexagonal structure. Aragonite and vaterite crystallize in orthorhombic structure. Following figures shows the unit cells of the three anhydrous crystalline forms: (Big balls indicate $\ce{Ca^{2+}}$ ions, small black and gray balls indicate C and O atoms, respectively.)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-5-fig1.png

5.1 Density of aragonite = $2.93\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$. Calculate the densities (in $\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$) of calcite and vaterite.

5.2 Determine the % change in volume in a crystalline $\ce{CaCO3}$ sample as it undergoes the following transitions.
i) from calcite to aragonite
ii) from aragonite to vaterite

5.3 Based on above calculations, which anhydrous crystalline form can become more stable than calcite at higher pressures?

The three anhydrous crystalline forms have lower solubility in water than amorphous $\ce{CaCO3}$. A plot of $\ln AP$ in solutions ($AP$ = product of activities of $\ce{Ca^{2+}(aq)}$ and $\ce{CO3^{2-}(aq)}$ in solution) that are in equilibrium with the different solid forms of $\ce{CaCO3}$ at different temperatures is given here.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-5-fig2.png

Adapted from J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 21 (2009) 425102 (6pp)

A sample of water was kept with calcite till equilibrium was reached. Then the supernatant was taken out in another container and was subjected to fast evaporation along with stirring at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ using suitable apparatus. Slow evaporation can lead to the formation of the crystalline phases before formation of amorphous phase.

5.4 After what percent reduction in water volume of the above supernatant (from calcite) at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, would amorphous $\ce{CaCO3}$ start precipitating?

The crystalline forms under suitable temperature and pressure conditions can also directly interconvert into each other.

5.5 Calculate the change in the molar entropy of $\ce{CaCO3}$ during the transformation of aragonite to calcite at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, given that the enthalpies of formation for calcite and aragonite are $-1206.9$ and $-1207.0\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, respectively (determined by calorimetry).

Though calcite is thermodynamically the most stable form of $\ce{CaCO3}$, many natural materials (e.g. conch shells and mollusk's shells) have predominantly aragonite form. It has been observed that the presence of cations in solution whose ionic size is larger than that of $\ce{Ca^{2+}}$ favour formation of aragonite phase.

5.6 Based on the above hypothesis, identify which of the following ions would facilitate the formation of aragonite phase: $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$, $\ce{Sr^{2+}}$, $\ce{Pb^{2+}}$, $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$, $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$

At a range of environmentally relevant temperatures (7.5 – $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$), particles of amorphous $\ce{CaCO3}$ rapidly dehydrate and crystallize to form particles of vaterite, which slowly transforms to calcite.

$$\text{Amorphous} \xrightarrow{\;k_1\;} \text{Vaterite} \xrightarrow{\;k_2\;} \text{Calcite}$$

The second stage of the transformation is approximately 10 times slower than the first. The rate constant for varterite to calcite transformation ($k_2$) at $10\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is $8.6\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. Assume no change in the solution that is in contact with the solid $\ce{CaCO3}$ during this time scale.

5.7 Assuming amorphous to calcite transformation as a sequence of consecutive unimolecular processes, calculate the mass percentages of amorphous and vaterite forms of the total $\ce{CaCO3}$ mass present after 30 min at $10\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Amount of vaterite $m_\mathrm{V}(t)$ at a particular time $t$ is given by,

$$m_V(t) = \frac{k_1}{k_2 - k_1}\left(e^{-k_1 t} - e^{-k_2 t}\right) m_A(0)$$

where, $k_1$ is the rate constant for the formation of vaterite from amorphous form and $m_\mathrm{A}(t)$ is the amount of amorphous form at time $t$.

5.8 If 1 kg of amorphous $\ce{CaCO3}$ had precipitated at $t = 0$, calculate (i) the time in which the maximum amount of vaterite would be observed, and (ii) the mass of this maximum amount of vaterite.

Dissolution of calcium carbonate

Scales of $\ce{CaCO3}$ are found in heated water boilers and pipelines. The hardest ones are due to calcite and aragonite forms. These can be removed by mechanically scrapping or chemically dissolving using acids and chelating agents such as EDTA (represented here as $\mathrm{H}_m\mathrm{Y}^{x-}$, $m$ = 0-4, $x$ = 4-0). The pH dependence of the initial rate of calcite dissolution in solutions of different pH (prepared using HCl, water and NaOH) in inert atmosphere and under stirring conditions is shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-5-fig3.png

Adapted from Chemical Geology, 42 (1984) 119—136

5.9 Identify whether each of the following statements can be inferred / cannot be inferred about dissolution of calcite from the above graph (Mark X in the appropriate box).
(i) There is no dissolution of calcite in solutions with pH > 5.3.
(ii) Dissolution of calcite follows an overall zero order kinetics at pH > 5.3.
(iii) Dissolution of calcite follows an overall first order kinetics below pH = 4.0.
(iv) Dissolution of calcite follows a second order kinetics with respect to $[\ce{H+}]$ in the pH range 4.0 – 5.0.
(v) Dissolution of calcite becomes faster with increasing solution pH.
(vi) $\ce{H2O}$ also has a dissolution pathway for calcite independent of $\ce{H+}$.

[In the printed table each statement has a Yes box and a No box.]

The following graph shows the effect of EDTA and pH on initial rates of calcite dissolution with respect to the stirring rate (rotating speed) in inert atmosphere. The pH of the EDTA and KCl solutions were adjusted using HCl (aq.) and NaOH (aq.).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-5-fig4.png

Adapted from Journal of Colloid and Interface Science 204(1998), 187–197.

Consider $r_\mathbf{Z}$, the initial rate of dissolution per unit surface area of calcite due to dissolving species $\mathbf{Z}$ with initial concentration $[\mathbf{Z}]$ in the solution, to be given by $r_\mathbf{Z} = k_\mathbf{Z}\,[\mathbf{Z}]$ where $k_\mathbf{Z}$ is the rate constant of the dissolution reaction due to species $\mathbf{Z}$. The $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}$ values of EDTA are 2.0, 2.7, 6.2 and 10.3, respectively. Assume that
(i) the predominant species dissolving calcite in the given solutions are $\ce{H+(aq)}$ and $\mathrm{H}_m\mathrm{Y}^{x-}\mathrm{(aq)}$ ($m$ = 0 – 4, $x$ = 4 – 0).
(ii) the rates of dissolution due to multiple species in a given system are additive.
(iii) at the given pH values, the predominant species of EDTA is present as almost 100% of the total EDTA concentration.

5.10 Determine the ratios of rate constants of dissolution due to $\ce{H2Y^{2-}(aq)}$, $\ce{Y^{4-}(aq)}$ and $\ce{H+(aq)}$ by considering the appropriate rates of dissolution at the rotating speed of $100\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$.

5.11 The following table has some statements related to the different forms and dissolution kinetics of $\ce{CaCO3}$. Choose the correct option for each pair of statements (from i - iv given below and mark X in the box):
• i. Statement A is correct and Statement B is wrong
• ii. Statement A is wrong and Statement B is correct
• iii. Both Statements A and B are correct and B is the reason for A
• iv. Both Statements A and B are correct and B is not the reason for A

a. Statement A: The transformation of aragonite to calcite is a thermodynamically feasible process.

Statement B: The transformation of aragonite to calcite is an enthalpy driven process.

b. Statement A: Dissolved $\ce{CaCO3}$ precipitates on the hotter regions of hot water pipes resulting in formation of scales.

Statement B: The solubility of $\ce{CaCO3}$ decreases with increase in temperature.

c. Statement A: The rate of dissolution of per mole of calcite will be more if its particle size is small.

Statement B: The rate of dissolution of calcite in acidic EDTA solution also depends on the ionic mobilities of $\ce{H+(aq)}$/EDTA(aq) species.

problems.title: Derivatizing Eugenol
problems.problem:
Problem 6 (15 marks). Derivatizing Eugenol

Eugenol ($\mathbf{A}$) is a compound present in cloves, tulsi, and many other plants. It is used to darken the colour of natural henna on skin. It is used in foods, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals as antimicrobial, analgesic and antioxidant.

Eugenol can be easily converted to 1-allyl-3,4-dimethoxybenzene ($\mathbf{B}$).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-6-fig1.png

6.1 From the following sets of reagents, identify which can be used for this conversion of $\mathbf{A}$ to $\mathbf{B}$. (Mark X in the correct box/es)
(a) $\ce{CH3I}$/$\ce{K2CO3}$
(b) $\ce{(CH3)2SO4}$/KOH
(c) $\ce{CH3I}$/$\ce{H2SO4}$
(d) $\ce{Me2SO}$/KOH
(e) $\ce{Me2S}$/$\ce{H2SO4}$

Several derivatives of Eugenol have been studied and have been found to have useful pharmaceutical properties. Here we will look at methods of obtaining two such derivatives.

Compound $\mathbf{B}$ can be oxidized with molar equivalent amounts of $\ce{OsO4}$ in aqueous medium to yield $\mathbf{C}$. However, toxicity and high cost of $\ce{OsO4}$ prevents its wider use despite high yield and selectivity. An different pathway was developed by an American chemist Barry Sharpless for the same transformation. This method uses fractional molar equivalents of $\ce{OsO4}$ (relative to the olefin) along with a few other reagents, listed on the arrow below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-6-fig2.png

The mixture is slightly turbid due to presence of small amount of non-aqueous phase in the system. A generic mechanism of this reaction is given below. $\mathbf{L}$ is a species which coordinates with the Os center facilitating the reaction, and $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ are two other species in the reaction mixture.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-6-fig3.png

6.2 i) Draw the structure of product $\mathbf{C}$.

ii) The overall reaction $\mathbf{B} \rightarrow \mathbf{C}$ can be classified as (Mark X in the appropriate box(es)):
a) redox reaction
b) addition reaction
c) hydrolysis reaction
d) acid base reaction

iii) List the species (both ionic and non-ionic) that will exist in the reaction flask at the end of reaction, other than the following: $\ce{H2O}$, $\ce{H+}$, $\ce{OH-}$, product $\mathbf{C}$

When the product $\mathbf{C}$ is treated with p-toluene sulfonyl chloride using the following procedure, a monoester $\mathbf{D}$ is produced as the single main product.

Step I: To a solution of compound $\mathbf{C}$ (1 mmol) in pyridine (2 mL), p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl, 1.1 mmol) was added at $0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The reaction mixture was stirred at $0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (for about 20-30 min) till the compound $\mathbf{C}$ was no more detected (using chromatography).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2020-6-fig4.png

Step II: Water (10 mL) was added to the reaction mixture followed by diethyl ether (5 mL), which led to formation of two layers in the reaction flask.

Step III: The ether layer was separated using a separating funnel. This ether solution was treated multiple times with 5% aq HCl (10 mL), followed by removal of the acidic layer.

Step IV: Finally, the ether layer was washed with 10% $\ce{NaHCO3}$ (aq) and then treated with anhydrous sodium sulphate (to remove water from the solution). The solvent was evaporated to produce $\mathbf{D}$ as the single product.

6.3 Write the structure of $\mathbf{D}$.

6.4 Which compound(s) were removed from the organic layer by using (i) water and (ii) HCl solution?

However, while carrying out the above procedure, a chemist forgot to treat the mixture with water in Step II and proceeded by adding diethyl ether, and then followed by Steps III and IV. The chemist identified two compounds $\mathbf{E}$ & $\mathbf{F}$ in the ether medium.

6.5 Identify $\mathbf{E}$ & $\mathbf{F}$

When compound $\mathbf{D}$ is treated with solid $\ce{K2CO3}$, compound $\mathbf{G}$ is formed.

problems.title: Persistent radical – TEMPO
problems.problem:
Problem 1 (18 marks). Persistent radical – TEMPO

Radicals are commonly known to be highly unstable due to their reactivity. However, in 1960, the synthesis and isolation of a stable radical, 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPO) changed this notion. Stable radicals are also called persistent radicals. TEMPO, a persistent radical is a red solid compound which has applications in organic synthesis and chemical analysis.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2021-1-fig1.png

Part A: The redox equilibria of TEMPO

1.1 Draw the resonance structure of TEMPO (including the lone pairs) other than the one shown above.

The redox reactions of TEMPO are known to be affected by the pH of the medium.

TEMPO undergoes one electron oxidation to yield species $\mathbf{A}$. TEMPO also undergoes reduction (accompanied by protonation) to give $\mathbf{B}$. $E^\circ_{(\mathbf{A}\to\text{TEMPO})} = 0.745\,\mathrm{V}$ (w.r.t. NHE) and $E^\circ_{(\text{TEMPO}\to\mathbf{B})} = 0.610\,\mathrm{V}$ (w.r.t. NHE).

1.2 Draw the structures of $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$.

1.3 Write the half-cell reaction and Nernst equation for the conversion of TEMPO to $\mathbf{B}$ (refer 1.2). Derive the relation between the reduction potential ($E$) of TEMPO and pH.

The stability of different redox species at specific potential and pH can be represented on a 2 dimensional plot as shown here for the TEMPO system. Such a plot is known as Pourbaix diagram. In this diagram, the regions between the lines represent conditions at which one particular species is thermodynamically more stable than all other species.

The lines represent equilibrium between two species (in this case at equal concentrations) under standard condition ($T = 298.15\,\mathrm{K}$). A horizontal line (line 1) separates species related by electron transfer process only. The slant lines (line 2 and 3) separate species related by both electron and proton transfers.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2021-1-fig2.png

1.4 Draw the structure of $\mathbf{C}$ and write the equilibrium process between the species (with the structures) separated by line 4 at pH = 7.4.

1.5 Derive the expression for the ratio $\dfrac{\text{slope (line 3)}}{\text{slope (line 2)}}$ starting from the corresponding Nernst equations and determine its value using the parameters involved.

A disproportionation reaction is one in which two identical units of a species react together to give a reduced and an oxidized species. (Reverse of this reaction is called comproportionation reaction). At pH < 3, TEMPO undergoes disproportionation reaction, yielding $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{C}$.

1.6 Write balanced equation for the disproportionation reaction and determine the equilibrium constant for the reaction at standard temperature? Show the main steps of calculations.

Part B: Using TEMPO in Electrochemical Oxidation

In reaction mixtures, the electrochemical potentials can also be modified by non-reacting species (such as ions) present in the system. Also the typical conditions, such as $[\ce{H+}]$ may be very different from standard values of $1\,\mathrm{M}$. In such situations, a formal potential $E^{\circ\prime}$ is defined for the system as the potential of the system at equilibrium where certain species are at certain (typical) specified concentrations. For the following, net concentration of TEMPO species is taken as $1\,\mathrm{mM}$, and pH as specified in each case.

One of the important applications of $\mathbf{A}$ is to mediate the electrochemical oxidation of primary and secondary alcohols under mildly basic aqueous conditions. The products of the reaction include aldehydes/ketones in high yields and $\mathbf{B}$, which is electrochemically converted back to $\mathbf{A}$. A typical setup for this reaction involves –

i) a “working electrode” – where the electrochemical regeneration of $\mathbf{A}$ takes place

ii) a counter electrode – for completion of the electrochemical circuit

In addition, a reference electrode is used for ensuring the absolute potentials of working and counter electrodes in the cell.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2021-1-fig3.png

1.7 Write the reaction taking place at the counter electrode and identify the anode and the cathode.

Mechanistic studies reveal that the oxidation of alcohol (ROH) proceeds through a nucleophilic attack of the alkoxide ion on $\mathbf{A}$.

1.8 Draw the structure of the most favorable intermediate formed after the nucleophillic attack.

After $\mathbf{A}$ is converted to $\mathbf{B}$ by alcohol, the species $\mathbf{A}$ is regenerated back from $\mathbf{B}$ in two steps:

Step i) conversion of $\mathbf{B}$ to TEMPO. If done electrochemically, it requires a formal potential of at least $E_2^{\circ\prime}$.

Step ii) conversion of TEMPO to $\mathbf{A}$. This requires a formal potential of at least $E_1^{\circ\prime}$.

For TEMPO in the above described cell, $E_1^{\circ\prime}$ doesn’t change with pH, whereas $E_2^{\circ\prime}$ changes with pH as shown in graph here.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2021-1-fig4.png

1.9 If the working electrode is operated at potential $E_1^{\circ\prime}$,

a) write the balanced equations for the possible pathways by which $\mathbf{B}$ is converted to TEMPO under the following conditions:

i) pH < 7     ii) pH > 7

b) Based on the above data, which of these conditions (i or ii) is expected to give higher conversion of alcohols to aldehydes/ketones per mol of $\mathbf{A}$ produced at the working electrode?

Introduction of functional groups to TEMPO can help in tuning its electrochemical properties. The effect of substituents on corresponding $E_1^{\circ\prime}$ values was studied for TEMPO analogs.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2021-1-fig5.png

1.10 Of the above three, write the analogs which are most likely to show pH-dependent $E_1^{\circ\prime}$ values in the pH range 2 to 7.

1.11 Arrange the values of $E_1^{\circ\prime}$ for substituted TEMPO analogs at pH 7 in order.

Graphs and diagrams are adapted from (Chem. Rev. 2018, 118, 4834−4885).

problems.title: Esters
problems.problem:
Problem 2 (14 marks). Esters

Many sweet-smelling compounds contain an ester functional group, R-CO-O-R′, where R/R′ = alkyl, aryl groups. Hydrolysis of an ester is an exhaustively studied reaction:

$$\ce{RCOOR' + H2O <=> RCOOH + R'OH}$$

The hydrolysis can be catalyzed by an acid (A) or a base (B). The reaction may be unimolecular (1) or bimolecular (2), and may involve breaking of acyl-O bond (AC) or alkyl-O bond (AL). Thus, there are eight different mechanisms possible as listed in the table below.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Acid catalyzed} & & \text{Base catalyzed} & \\ \hline \text{Unimolecular} & \text{Bimolecular} & \text{Unimolecular} & \text{Bimolecular} \\ \hline \mathrm{A_{AC}1} & \mathrm{A_{AC}2} & \mathrm{B_{AC}1} & \mathrm{B_{AC}2} \\ \hline \mathrm{A_{AL}1} & \mathrm{A_{AL}2} & \mathrm{B_{AL}1} & \mathrm{B_{AL}2} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

The mechanism in a given reaction depends on the structure of the ester and the reaction conditions.

2.1 Consider the acidic hydrolysis of methylpentanoate in aqueous $\ce{H2SO4}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2021-2-fig1.png

In the hydrolysis using moderately concentrated $\ce{H2SO4}$, two additional compounds $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{S}$ (other than the expected alcohol and carboxylic acid) having identical molecular formulae are formed in small amounts.

i) Draw the structures of $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{S}$.

ii) When the hydrolysis is carried out in aqueous ethanol containing $\ce{H2SO4}$, another compound $\mathbf{T}$ which is not an acid/alcohol/ester is also formed. Identify $\mathbf{T}$.

Draw the structure of cationic intermediate $\mathbf{V}$ and neutral compound $\mathbf{W}$ formed in concentrated acid before pouring into water.

2.6. An ester can also be hydrolyzed by heating with aqueous $\ce{NaOH}$ followed by acidification to yield the carboxylic acid. For alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl benzoate labeled with $\ce{^{18}O}$, the rate of hydrolysis depends on the concentrations of both ester and alkali.

problems.title: Ozone in Troposphere
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (16 marks). Ozone in Troposphere

In recent decades, tropospheric ozone is being observed in higher concentrations, particularly in urban atmospheres. At concentrations above 70 ppb (parts per billion by mass), ozone is hazardous for our health and environment. Carbon monoxide, volatile organic compounds, hydroxyl radical and nitrogen oxides ($\ce{NO}_x$) are some of the major components of exhaust gases from vehicles. In presence of near-UV solar radiation (325 nm to 450 nm), a series of reactions among these gases produces significant amount of ozone in the troposphere.

3.1 In the following steps (i to v) showing one such reaction sequence (all gaseous species), write the species $\mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{c}$, $\mathbf{d}$, $\mathbf{e}$ (Coefficients of given species should not be changed). Write the net reaction from steps i) to v).

i) $\ce{CO} + \ce{HO}^{\bullet} \rightarrow \mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}$

ii) $\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} \rightarrow {}^{\bullet}\ce{O2H}$

iii) ${}^{\bullet}\ce{O2H} + \ce{NO} \rightarrow \mathbf{d} + \mathbf{e}$

iv) $\mathbf{d}$ (sunlight 325 nm – 450 nm) $\rightarrow \ce{NO + O}$

v) The oxygen radical reacts with oxygen molecule to form ozone.

The ozone formed in troposphere is also degraded by the following reaction:

$$\ce{NO + O3 -> NO2 + O2}$$

If oxygen radicals are present in air, $\ce{NO2}$ can convert into NO.

$$\ce{NO2 + O -> NO + O2}$$

The gases CO, $\ce{NO}_x$ and $\ce{O3}$ are tropospheric air pollutants. Their concentrations at one location may change over time of the day, and also over seasons.

About the above mentioned atmospheric gases, following facts are available with us.

Facts:

(R1) During day time, it is sunlight rather than high temperature that leads to more free radical production as compared to that during night time.

(R2) Colder days have lower convection currents in air and hence, have lower mixing and dilution of gases from different zones in local atmosphere.

(R3) Winter days can have higher relative humidity than summer days inspite of having lower absolute humidity.

(R4) Acidic gases react with atmospheric water and come to ground in rainwater.

(R5) $\ce{NO}_x$ facilitate decay of ozone.

(R6) $\ce{NO}_x$ facilitate production of ozone.

(R7) Slope of concentration vs time graph for a gas indicates difference of production rate and decay rate of that gas.

Following figure shows tropospheric concentration of CO, $\ce{NO}_x$, and ozone in air recorded in Pune city, in India in a year. Time 0 is midnight. Vertical lines in the plot indicate variations in the concentrations of the gases over the month. The values may be considered typical of the given months in any year.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/in-2021-3-fig1.png

Based on the information provided above and the tropospheric concentration of CO, $\ce{NO}_x$, and ozone in air in Pune city as given in the graphs in page 8, certain statements (S1-S5) are given below which may be Correct or Incorrect for the Pune site.

S1. Amount of water vapour in the air does not affect ozone concentration.

S2. Ratio of $\ce{NO2}$: NO in the air is higher at 8 p.m. than at 8 a.m.

S3. Higher concentration of CO in the month of November is an evidence of higher production rates of the gases than in the month of May.

S4. Rate of ozone buildup increases with increase in temperature.

S5. Observed lifetime of ozone during day time is much longer than that of $\ce{NO}_x$ and CO.
